findings.passage: Voter ID laws are strategies to prevent communities of color from having access to ballots and participating in this democratic process.
findings.note: Senate office press release (sent 2018-06-28) giving her floor comments on House Bill 1092, a constitutional amendment requiring photo ID to vote. She also says it burdens seniors and that more than 300,000 registered voters in North Carolina do not have a photo ID.

findings.passage: Seniors with disabilities find accessibility at polls difficult, and when asked to show their IDs, they feel disenfranchised.
findings.note: Same release; she also says retired seniors who stopped driving are unlikely to renew a driver's license and, if their ID is expired, cannot register to vote.
Her office's release states: Senator Waddell voted against House Bill 1092, the constitutional amendment requiring photo ID for in-person voting.

findings.passage: It is important that measures in our voting process remain accessible to all citizens in North Carolina.
findings.note: Press release in her name, sent 2018-06-22, on the proposed photo-ID amendment (HB 1092); she says she opposes hindrance to the voting process already in existence.

findings.passage: Voter ID laws are strategies — that’s what it seems like it is — to prevent communities of color from having access to ballots, and participating in this democratic process,
findings.note: Carolina Journal quotes her on the photo-ID amendment; the passage is the outlet's quote of her, ending with a comma before the attribution.

findings.passage: This law does not create adequate fail-safe mechanisms to protect the right of every eligible North Carolinian to vote.
findings.note: Senate office release on the Senate vote to override the governor's veto of SB 824 (voter ID implementation); she also says the bill risks keeping voters from exercising their right. The same release says she voted against SB 824.
